abstract: Given the severe negative impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the economy, and the key role played by firm resilience in recovering from the adverse impacts of external shocks. This paper constructs a panel dataset of alumni relations between listed companies in China based on executives’ educational backgrounds and uses social network analysis to investigate the effects of executive alumni networks on firm resilience. We find that during the COVID-19 pandemic, firms in the centre of the alumni network had significantly higher net operating cash flow than other firms. Moreover, this effect is more pronounced for firms located in regions with high COVID-19 exposure or with greater operational uncertainty. Through mechanism analysis, the study demonstrates that alumni networks stabilize net operating cash flow by ensuring efficient product circulation and obtaining increased commercial credit for the firm. Our findings contribute to the emerging literature on profiting from alumni networks and carry crucial implications for managers regarding managing the impact of uncertainty.

abstract: Research on the ‘hot hand’ phenomenon still continues four decades after the initial study by Gilovich et al. (1985). Here, we examine the existence of excessive streakiness by American horse jockeys. As a whole, American horse jockeys clearly display excessive streakiness. Individually, up to one-third of jockeys in our dataset can be said to exhibit excessive streakiness over their racing records. While utilizing this information leads to higher returns to wagering (i.e. less negative), profitable wagering opportunities surrounding streakiness do not exist.
title: Making it rein? Hot hands, wagering markets and American horse jockeys

abstract: This study investigates the role of industrial coagglomeration in promoting high-quality economic development using panel data from 30 Chinese provinces between 2012 and 2021. Employing a two-way fixed effects model, we find that coagglomeration significantly enhances development quality, a result that remains robust to alternative model specifications and instrumental variable estimation. Mechanism analysis demonstrates that coagglomeration facilitates high-quality development through two critical pathways: greater openness to foreign trade and enhanced network infrastructure. Heterogeneity analysis further reveals that these positive effects are more pronounced in regions with stronger technological innovation capacity richer human capital, and a more developed service sector. In contrast, the effects are statistically insignificant in regions constrained by weaker technological foundations, lower labour quality and less developed service systems, suggesting that structural bottlenecks may inhibit the realization of coagglomeration externalities. By identifying multidimensional transmission mechanisms and regional heterogeneity, this study deepens the theoretical understanding of how industrial spatial organization shapes development quality and provides empirical foundations for designing regionally differentiated development strategies.

abstract: ABSTRACT Resilience is still conceptualised as gender‐neutral in research and policy discussions. However, a gendered resilience framework suggests that gender roles and intra‐household dynamics are intricately linked with household resilience. This manuscript aims to analyse the effect of gender role attitudes on climate change resilience. The study uses the ‘Life in Kyrgyzstan’ survey for four waves between 2012 and 2019. The estimation employs latent profile analysis (LPA) to identify homogeneous profiles based on gender role attitudes. The findings from the LPA approach produce three homogeneous clusters: ‘Low Egalitarian’, ‘Medium Egalitarian’ and ‘High Egalitarian’ profiles. The estimation strategy also incorporates the Resilience Index Measurement Analysis (RIMA) framework to construct the Resilience Capacity Index (RCI), based on four pillars: Access to Basic Services (ABS), Assets (AST), Social Safety Nets (SSN) and Adaptive Capacity (AC). To examine the potential causal relationship between gender role attitudes and resilience, the manuscript utilises a cross‐lagged panel model approach. Findings confirm that more egalitarian attitudes or moving from a ‘Low Egalitarian’ to a ‘High Egalitarian’ profile positively affect household resilience pillars, particularly through AC and SSN. The findings support the development of a policy that promotes a gendered approach to climate change resilience in Kyrgyzstan.
abstract_zh: 摘要 在研究和政策讨论中，韧性仍被视为性别中立的。然而，性别化韧性框架表明，性别角色和家庭内部动态与家庭韧性密切相关。本文旨在分析性别角色态度对气候变化韧性的影响。研究使用了2012年至2019年间四波“吉尔吉斯斯坦生活”调查数据。估计采用潜在剖面分析（LPA）来基于性别角色态度识别同质剖面。LPA方法的结果产生了三个同质聚类：“低平等主义”、“中等平等主义”和“高平等主义”剖面。估计策略还结合了韧性指数测量分析（RIMA）框架，基于四个支柱构建韧性能力指数（RCI）：基本服务获取（ABS）、资产（AST）、社会安全网（SSN）和适应能力（AC）。为考察性别角色态度与韧性之间潜在的因果关系，本文采用交叉滞后面板模型方法。研究结果证实，更平等的态度或从“低平等主义”向“高平等主义”剖面的转变对家庭韧性支柱产生积极影响，尤其是通过AC和SSN。这些发现支持在吉尔吉斯斯坦制定促进性别化气候变化韧性方法的政策。
journal: Australian Journal of Agricultural and Resource Economics
title: Gender‐Sensitive Resilience in Kyrgyz Households: Latent Profile and Cross‐Lagged Dynamic Panel Approaches
title_zh: 吉尔吉斯斯坦家庭中的性别敏感韧性：潜在剖面与交叉滞后动态面板方法

abstract: We propose “Taylor rule yields” across horizons for the United States. Applying the standard Taylor rule to expected paths of inflation and the output gap, we construct a sequence of short‐term rates under neutral monetary policy stances, whose average defines the Taylor rule yield at each horizon. Taylor rule deviations (TRDs), the gaps between market‐expected rates and these yields, excluding risk premia, capture the effective stance of monetary policy even under the effective lower bound (ELB). TRDs also help disentangle the role of the ELB from other factors, offering insight into the severity and nature of the policy constraint.
abstract_zh: 我们针对美国提出了跨期限的“泰勒规则收益率”。将标准泰勒规则应用于预期通胀路径和产出缺口，我们构建了在中性货币政策立场下的一系列短期利率序列，其平均值定义了各期限的泰勒规则收益率。泰勒规则偏差（TRDs），即市场预期利率与这些收益率之间的差额（剔除风险溢价），即使在有效下限（ELB）条件下也能捕捉货币政策的实际立场。TRDs还有助于将ELB的作用与其他因素区分开来，为政策约束的严重性和性质提供洞见。
journal: Journal of Money, Credit and Banking
title: Taylor Rule Deviations Across Horizons: A Practical Tool for Monetary Policy
title_zh: 跨期限泰勒规则偏离：货币政策实用工具
